turns.response_html:
Based on the technical labels in the image, you actually have two identical power bricks in terms of their capabilities, with one tiny difference in how much power they can pull from your wall outlet. Both are high-quality, high-output LG adapters.

Here is the breakdown of their specifications and which monitor you should plug them into.

The Specifications

Which one goes where?

Because both bricks output the exact same $19.5\text{ V}$ at $10.8\text{ A}$ ($210.6\text{ W}$), they are technically interchangeable for your monitors. They deliver the exact same amount of power to the display.

However, looking at the input ratings (the power they draw from your wall outlet):

  • The Top Adapter is rated for a maximum input of $3.0\text{ A}$. This suggests it might have a slightly different internal component layout or efficiency curve that allows for a higher maximum draw under heavy transient loads.
  • The Bottom Adapter is rated for a maximum input of $2.5\text{ A}$.

💡 Recommendation

  • Plug the TOP adapter into your Gaming Monitor. Gaming monitors (especially high-refresh-rate, OLED, or ultrawide models) experience rapid changes in brightness and refresh rates, causing sharp spikes in power demand. The slightly higher input current tolerance makes this brick ideal for handling those aggressive fluctuations.
  • Plug the BOTTOM adapter into your Work Monitor. Standard work monitors typically have a much more stable, consistent, and lower overall power draw profile.
